page: Amazon Web Services m8azn.metal-12xl is a bare-metal, general-purpose server type driven by the AMD EPYC 9R05 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated physical cores operating at 5.0 GHz with one thread per core, completely bypassing hypervisor virtualization overhead. The platform provides 192.0 GB of DDR5 memory rated at 6 GHz, maintaining a balanced general-purpose allocation of 4.0 GB per core. Networking bandwidth offers a baseline of 100 Gbps, while local instance storage is absent, necessitating network-attached EBS volumes for persistence. Hardware acceleration includes AVX-512 extensions (VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration flags such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results place the m8azn.metal-12xl consistently within the top tier. In raw compute tests, it achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 3156.0 and a multi-core score of 32996.0, coupled with a PassMark CPU score of 116193.1 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 201425.18. Memory throughput is substantial, measuring 530.58 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 200.67 GB/sec for large-block writes. This memory subsystem performance is reflected in in-memory benchmarks, where Redis SET operations reach 178.57 million operations per second, alongside a static web serving throughput of 120.26 GB/sec.

The bare-metal configuration provides high compute efficiency and dedicated resource isolation without virtualization contention. However, workloads requiring dense local NVMe storage must account for the reliance on remote storage, and absence of dedicated GPUs limits accelerated processing to vector instruction sets on the host CPU. The platform is well suited for demanding enterprise applications, memory-resident key-value caching, intensive data compression, high-throughput web serving, and Clang-based compilation workflows.
description: Amazon Web Services m8azn.metal-12xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by a 48-core AMD EPYC 9R05 processor running at 5.0 GHz on x86_64 architecture. It provides 192.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 6 GHz, offering a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per dedicated physical core with no hypervisor layer. The instance delivers a 100 Gbps network baseline and relies entirely on external storage, as no local storage is included. Benchmarks confirm top-tier performance across raw compute, extended vector operations (PassMark extended instructions at 149161.82), and high-throughput workloads, achieving 178.57 million Redis SET operations per second and 120.26 GB/sec in static web serving. This server is optimized for high-performance enterprise workloads, Clang code compilation, large-scale Redis in-memory caches, and web infrastructure requiring dedicated single-threaded core execution.
